title: Cottage Pie
subtitle: British minced beef and vegetable pie under a mashed potato topping
excerpt: The classic British comfort dish: a rich, savoury beef mince filling topped with smooth, buttery mash and baked until golden. Proper, unfussy home cooking.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from classic British cottage pie preparations.

recipe.freezeNotes: Assemble fully and freeze unbaked. Bake from frozen at 180 C for 1 hour, covered with foil for the first 40 minutes, then uncovered to brown.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well; use a larger roasting tin or two separate dishes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to 2 days ahead, cover and refrigerate. Bring to room temperature for 30 minutes before baking, or add 10 minutes to the baking time.
recipe.temperatureNote: Fan 180 C. The high heat is for the mash topping to brown; the filling is already cooked.

content.text: Brown the mince in batches and let it colour properly before adding liquid. The filling should be moist but not swampy: simmer uncovered at the end to reduce if needed. Mash the potato while hot and season it assertively. Do not skimp on the Worcestershire sauce.

items.prepNote: floury variety such as Maris Piper, peeled and cut into chunks

content.text: Brown the mince. Heat the oil in a large saucepan over high heat. Add the beef mince in a single layer; do not stir for 3 minutes so it browns on the bottom rather than steaming. Break up and continue cooking for another 3 minutes until all moisture has evaporated and the meat is deep brown in places. Remove to a plate.

Cook the vegetables. In the same pan over medium heat, add the onion, carrot and celery. Cook for 8 to 10 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and cook for 2 minutes. Add the tomato puree and cook for 2 minutes, stirring.

Make the sauce. Return the browned mince to the pan. Sprinkle over the flour and stir to coat. Pour in the beef stock and Worcestershire sauce. Add the thyme and bay leaves. Bring to the boil, then simmer over medium-low heat for 20 to 25 minutes until the sauce is thick and coats the mince. It should not be liquid. Remove the bay leaves. Stir in the frozen peas. Season well.

Make the mash. While the filling cooks, boil the potatoes in salted water until completely tender, about 20 minutes. Drain and return to the pan over low heat for 2 minutes to drive off steam. Pass through a ricer or sieve, or mash very thoroughly. Beat in the butter and warm milk until the mash is smooth and creamy but still firm enough to hold its shape. Season with salt and white pepper.

Preheat the oven to 200 C (fan 180 C). Tip the beef filling into a roasting tin or deep ovenproof dish roughly 25 cm x 20 cm. Spread the mash evenly over the top, starting at the edges to seal in the filling, and working towards the centre. Use a fork to rake the surface into ridges: these will catch the heat and crisp up.

Scatter over the grated cheddar if using. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the top is golden brown and the filling is bubbling at the edges. Rest for 10 minutes before serving: the filling is very hot and resting allows it to set slightly so it does not flood when portioned.

items.symptom: Mash sinks into the filling when spreading
items.cause: The mash is too soft and wet, or the filling is too hot and loose.
items.fix: Make a stiffer mash by using less milk. Let the filling cool for 10 minutes before topping: a cooler, thicker filling supports the mash better.

items.symptom: Filling floods out from under the mash during baking
items.cause: Too much liquid in the filling, or the mash did not seal to the edges of the dish.
items.fix: Make sure the filling is reduced and quite thick before topping. Spread the mash firmly to the very edges of the dish to seal it.

items.symptom: Mash topping is pale after the full cooking time
items.cause: No cheese on top, or the oven temperature was too low.
items.fix: Switch the oven to grill for the last 3 to 5 minutes, watching closely. Adding grated cheddar on top ensures reliable browning even without the grill.

items.cause: Insufficient browning on the mince, or not enough seasoning in the sauce.
items.fix: Taste the filling before topping and adjust: more salt, more Worcestershire sauce, a small splash of soy sauce to deepen the savouriness.
